issue: Under U.S.S.G. § 4B1.2(b), must a court use a categorical approach that compares a prior state drug conviction to the federal drug schedules, or a state-dependent approach that does not turn on federal schedules?

sides.position: Categorical approach: a prior state drug conviction qualifies as a 'controlled substance offense' only if the state drug schedule matches the federal schedule, applying the categorical approach as in Taylor.
cases: United States v. Townsend, 897 F.3d 66 (2d Cir. 2018)
United States v. Gibson, 55 F.4th 153 (2d Cir. 2022)
United States v. Chaires, 88 F.4th 172 (2d Cir. 2023)

sides.position: State-dependent approach: section 4B1.2(b) does not turn on the content of federal drug schedules or their match with a state-law analog.
cases: United States v. Jones, 81 F.4th 591 (6th Cir. 2023)
United States v. Chaires, 88 F.4th 172 (2d Cir. 2023)

this_court: The Second Circuit applies the categorical approach, as binding under Townsend. The concurrence says it continues to believe the state-dependent approach is the correct reading.
quote: Indeed, six of our sister circuits have already concluded as much, holding that section 4B1.2(b) calls for a statedependent approach rather than a categorical one.
cite: United States v. Chaires, 88 F.4th 172 (2d Cir. 2023)
